sheet.summary: India's domestic cotton deficit is set to widen past 9 million bales as adverse El Nino weather hurts crop output while export demand under new trade pacts picks up pace. To offset tight domestic availability, mills imported a record 7.1 million bales in 2025-26, yet raw cotton and yarn costs have continued to climb. For salaried Indian households, this persistent raw material squeeze raises manufacturing costs across mills and will ultimately translate into higher retail prices for everyday garments, school uniforms, and festive clothing.

Cotton imports hit a record high in 2025-26 to an estimated 7.1 million bales of 170 kilograms compared to last year's imports of 5.74 million bales. Prices have also risen more than 7% in the past month.
topic.title: Cotton shortage set to worsen as new deals drive export demand
